children: WINNIPEG — Canola futures on the Intercontinental Exchange exited the weekend on a low note, pressured by weaker comparable oil prices and farmer selling.
Crude oil was in negative territory after the United States lifted sanctions on Russian oil. However, conflicts in Ukraine and the Middle East are ongoing.
Chicago soyoil and European rapeseed were in the red on Monday, while Malaysian palm oil was higher after the drought-stricken Kapuas River in Indonesia caused shipping issues.
Statistics Canada reported the country's annual inflation rate was 3.1 per cent in September, compared to 3.0 per cent in August.
Alberta's canola harvest was 74 per cent complete as of Oct. 13.
At mid-afternoon, the Canadian dollar was up nearly three-tenths of a U.S. cent compared to Friday's close.
There were 99,595 canola contracts traded on Monday, compared to Friday when 113,995 contracts changed hands. Spreads accounted for 63,052 contracts in today's trade.
